newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot power prices up at COB, Southwest weaker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot power prices up at COB, Southwest weaker.

text.p: Spot power prices at the California-Oregon border (COB) were marginally higher amid some buying interest from northern California utilities, trade sources said Thursday.
"This is probably a short-term phenomenon," related to flood control measures on the region's river system, said one California trader.
Heavy rain and flooding in the Pacific Northwest and northern California have led to flow cutbacks at major hydroelectric dams, but the extra water is expected to be released starting next week.
"The emphasis now is more on controlling the water than generating power," said a spokesman for San Francisco-based Pacific Gas and Electric Co.
But prices in the Southwest were seen lower amid balmy temperatures and weaker spot natural gas prices.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Friday was quoted $14.00-16.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), up from $13.50-14.50 before the New Year holiday.
Off-peak COB for Friday was quoted $9.00-10.00, up from lows near $8.00 early in the week.
Friday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was lower at $12.00-$13.00, while off-peak was at $9.00-10.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Friday was quoted $13.00-15.00, little changed from Tuesday.
Off-peak PV for Friday was also steady at $9.00-10.00 per MWh.
Friday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were also quoted $13.00-15.00, with off-peak at $8.00-9.00.
